origin.name: B(L)IND
origin.description: A dating app that arranges blind dates between random people. Its name holds both BLIND and BIND in the same word. It brought Aarna and Mukund to the same cafe table in Chicago three years ago; choosing to meet again was their decision.

profiles.name: Aarna
profiles.tagline: She notices what a room feels like before she notices what needs fixing.
profiles.gesture: She leaves a doorway unfinished in her sketchbook and rests her hand on the back of his neck as she passes.

sections.title: Her world
paragraphs: Aarna is a painter living with Mukund in a three-bedroom downtown Chicago apartment overlooking the river. They moved in together during their second year. They share one bedroom and have a separate workspace each.

She has spent a year preparing her first major solo exhibition. She thinks through paintings in a sketchbook, sometimes returning to the same doorway without erasing an earlier attempt. Painting is her work, not simply shorthand for being emotional.

sections.title: Home, family and education
paragraphs: Her family is originally from India and settled in the United States. Her parents live in New Jersey, where they own a shop selling musical instruments.
She graduated from college in New York state and now lives in Chicago. Her university, degree, family names and exact hometown in New Jersey have not been specified.

She and Mukund both have cars now. For a year he drove her to work, errands and other places. The reason she did not drive then remains unspecified; the draft remembers a large roll of art paper that would barely fit in his car.

sections.title: Their everyday life
paragraphs: They mostly eat out and sometimes cook together on weekends. They watch Hindi, English and Telugu films, listen to songs, and take night walks beside the river.
At home she sketches and thinks through painting ideas while Mukund reads. They can share a quiet room without sharing the same activity.

sections.title: A settled past
paragraphs: Aarna and Mukund have both had previous relationships. They discussed that history early and left it in the past. Ex-partners do not intrude, compete with the current relationship, or explain away the disagreement in this story.

sections.title: What she brings
paragraphs: She can make another person feel specifically seen. Her affection lives in small observations, private jokes, and the ability to stay with something that does not immediately make sense.
She is capable of sustained practical effort. The exhibition required savings, applications, frames, and persistence; needing comfort does not erase that competence.

sections.title: Where she struggles
paragraphs: Aarna has a short temper. When she feels unheard, she can return to the same point and sharpen her words while trying to get a response that feels right. She is responsible for how she speaks, even when her hurt is understandable.
She can be capable with bookings and everyday tasks while still needing someone to sit with her disappointment. The story does not treat those needs as contradictory.

sections.title: How she loves
paragraphs: She remembers his habits and makes room for his ordinary presence. She values the occasions when his practical help has made a difference, even when the same response is not what she needs today.
Emotional closeness, for her, includes being allowed to be uncertain, unproductive, and visibly upset without having to recover on someone else's schedule.

sections.title: The first meeting
paragraphs: B(L)IND arranged their random blind date three years ago. In the current draft, she arrives at a cafe with paint on her wrist; Mukund asks what she has been making. The conversation lasts beyond their coffee.
The app and the blind-date origin are approved story facts. The cafe, paint mark, and dialogue are editable first-draft details.

sections.title: What this weekend asks of her
paragraphs: Friday's cancellation takes away both an exhibition and the celebration they had planned. The ordinary dinner and walk home continue while their argument rises and falls.

When Mukund's brother calls about their mother's mild heart attack, Aarna travels with Mukund to San Jose on Saturday. She drives to the airport, listens on the flight, and stays beside him. Her gallery loss still matters; the emergency does not cancel it.

After they know his mother is doing well, they settle their argument in the hospital lobby on Saturday night. Both apologize and agree on how to respond differently. They end by hugging, without requiring Aarna's grief about the exhibition to be over.

profiles.name: Mukund
profiles.tagline: He reaches for a next step because standing still can feel like letting someone down.
profiles.gesture: He uncovers his book and keeps her place in the sketchbook with an unopened envelope.

sections.title: His world
paragraphs: Mukund moved to Chicago for work after graduating from college in California. He works in medical sales; the exact medical-device or pharmaceutical specialty has not been fixed.

He lives with Aarna in a three-bedroom downtown apartment overlooking the Chicago River. They moved in together during their second year, share a bedroom, and each have a home workspace. He also reads in a chair beside the river-view window.

sections.title: Home, family and education
paragraphs: His family is originally from India and settled in the United States. His mother and elder brother live in San Jose, California. His brother is a software engineer.
His mother makes podcasts interviewing celebrities and other prominent people around the country, mostly Indian celebrities and public figures settled in the United States.

He graduated in California before moving to Chicago for his job. No specific university, campus, degree or family names have been established. His mother's podcast introduction is part of an ordinary family exchange at the beginning of the draft.

sections.title: Their everyday life
paragraphs: Mukund reads books for pleasure and listens to songs, sometimes singing an old film tune incorrectly. He and Aarna see Hindi, English and Telugu films, usually eat out, and sometimes cook together on weekends.

They each have a car now. For a year he drove Aarna to work and other places, often reading while waiting. Night walks beside the river and quiet time with his book and her sketchbook are familiar routines.

sections.title: A settled past
paragraphs: Mukund and Aarna have both had previous relationships. Neither keeps that history secret or makes the other compete with it. No ex-partner returns, and their current misunderstanding is not a love triangle.

sections.title: What he brings
paragraphs: He comes when Aarna calls, remembers details, and helps with the unglamorous work around her painting. He is capable of warmth and humour, not just efficiency.
He likes old film songs and keeps singing one with the same wrong note, despite knowing several recordings by heart. Not everything he enjoys has to be useful or improved.

sections.title: Where he struggles
paragraphs: Mukund usually keeps his temper, but can become frustrated and occasionally raise his voice when the same disagreement keeps returning. That is not an excuse for speaking harshly; he acknowledges and apologizes for it.
He can mistake a useful action for the support Aarna needs at that moment. When his mother is hospitalized, he also discovers how little reassurance a practical answer can provide when fear remains.

sections.title: How he loves
paragraphs: Through reliability, attention, effort, and ordinary acts: driving her places, saving her sketchbook page, remembering which restaurant seat keeps her out of the draft.
He wants Aarna's work to find its audience. Learning to wait beside her disappointment is an addition to that care, not a rejection of every useful thing he has done.

sections.title: The first meeting
paragraphs: B(L)IND placed him on a blind date with Aarna three years ago. In the current draft he arrives early, wearing blue, and asks about the paint on her wrist instead of opening with a job-title question.
The pairing was random. The three years that followed were made of choices, not proof that an app knew they were destined for each other.

sections.title: What this weekend asks of him
paragraphs: His brother calls on Friday night to say their mother has had a mild heart attack and is receiving hospital care in San Jose. By Saturday night the doctor has confirmed she is doing well after treatment; she remains under observation with recovery and follow-up care to discuss.
On Saturday's flight he accepts Aarna's presence without treating it as proof that Friday's disagreement is over. Their conversation begins the repair, but does not finish it.

With the immediate worry eased, they settle the conflict in the hospital lobby and end in an embrace. He acknowledges not listening and agrees to ask before acting; she takes responsibility for pressing the argument instead of stating her need.
